text:
alyssa: Quick recap from the replay harness + autoscale runs we did on dedicated-pool-e. Key takeaways below.

mike: Thanks — can you paste the exact harness config? want to reproduce locally.

alyssa: Sure. We used the replay harness that samples from prod traces (2025-11-10 -> 2025-11-12), rate-multiplier=2, seq-dist from histograms. Config:
```json
{"workload":"chat","rate_multiplier":2,"seq_p95":512,"kv_cache_hit":0.6,"batch_target_ms":20}
```

tara: Nice. Did you pin kernel versions? last time kernel changes shifted perf by ~10%.

alyssa: Yes — runtime v1.12.3 with kernel-selection=v2 (heuristic allowing mixed int8/fp16 for attention). We also forced continuous batching on for the run.

perf-bot: Run summary (dedicated-pool-e, 8xA100):
- steady RPS: 320
- median p95 latency: 210ms -> exceeded target 180ms
- cold-starts observed: 6 during scale-up window
- cache hit rate: 0.61

infra-bot: Autoscale timeline snippets (timestamps are relative seconds):
```
0s: 4 instances
30s: queue spike -> scale request
72s: new instance ready (scale-up latency 42s)
120s: traffic sustained -> additional scale
```

mike: Scale-up 42s seems high. Is that OS boot or model load time? logs?

alyssa: Mostly model weight mmap + kernel JIT warmup. Profile excerpt:
```
[model_load] mmap weights: 8.3s
[kernel_jit] compile krylov ops: 10.1s
[init_cache] allocate KV buffers: 2.7s
[serve_ready] register routes: 0.9s
```

kevin: What about batching heuristics? did we see ineffective small batches during burst?

alyssa: Yes. During ramp we had lots of small batches ~batch_size 3 because of hard window=20ms. Adjusting to adaptive window (20ms -> 40ms when queue>50) increased batch_size to ~11 and reduced token-cost by 14% with 5% p95 latency improvement.

tara: Any evidence the KV cache eviction policy caused regressions? we saw earlier cache thrashing.

alyssa: We had TTL-based eviction set to 300s. Replay had many unique prefixes; cache hit stayed ~0.61. When we ran a follow-up with LRU and larger pool the hit shot to 0.78 and p95 improved 18ms. But memory footprint increased 22%.

mike: Good tradeoff data. Can we get an apples-to-apples comparison doc with same model+hardware and only one variable changed per run?

alyssa: Yep — next step: create matrix with dims [kernel-selection (v1/v2), batching(window static/adaptive), cache(policy ttl/lru, size), autoscale(min/max)] and run 6h sweeps. I'll schedule on dedicated-pool-f for isolated runs.

kevin: Also capture per-token CPU/GPU utilization and kernel-level counters. We need that to debug the JIT warmup cost.

alyssa: Adding perf counters and a short profiler script. Posting dashboard link when ready: https://dash.internal.redwood/perf/replay/1764507890

tara: Awesome. One last ask — please capture burst-credit usage for dedicated pools. We had weird throttles last quarter.

alyssa: Noted. Will include burst-credit graphs and raw traces. Planning to start runs tomorrow 03:00 UTC. cc @mike @kevin

mike: :thumbsup:
